title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse + pinning optimizations
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Improves paged KV cache block allocator reuse and pinning to reduce evictions and improve throughput/latency for long-context workloads; no API changes.
description: Context: long-context workloads were observing eviction thrashing and allocator churn in the paged KV cache which increased tail latency and reduced throughput. Motivation: reduce allocator churn and avoid unnecessary evictions by reusing freed blocks, introducing a lightweight pinning mechanism, and making the allocator LRU-aware. This PR implements a block reuse pool in the paged KV cache allocator, adds per-block pin counts with fast-path checks to prevent eviction of recently pinned blocks, and improves bookkeeping to reduce fragmentation. Key changes: 1) allocator now maintains reusable block lists keyed by block size and device so freed blocks are re-used before allocating new memory; 2) pinned_blocks module introduces pin counts and integrates with the eviction policy to prefer evicting unpinned and cold blocks; 3) block_manager integrates reuse pool with the background defragmentation job and reduces expensive atomic ops in the hot path; 4) added telemetry: new metrics (kv_block_reuse_hits, kv_block_pin_evictions, kv_block_fragmentation_ratio) and tracing spans around allocate/free/pin/unpin; 5) added deterministic unit and stress tests plus microbench harness for throughput and p95 latency under synthetic streaming workloads. Benchmarks: on internal Llama2-13B streaming workload with 8k context, measured sustained throughput +12% and p95 latency -15% versus baseline; allocation-related CPU usage down ~25% in the runtime; mem fragmentation ratio improved ~18%. Testing/CI: unit/integration tests added and flakiness addressed (integration rerun once), benchmarks committed but gated (benchmarks do not run on CI by default). Rollout: default behavior enabled behind runtime flag runtime.kv_cache.reuse_pool_enabled=true; we plan a staged rollout (canary -> 50% -> 100%) with alerting on kv_block_pin_evictions and regressed p95. Backwards compatibility: no customer-facing API changes; config flag allows rollback. Notes: paid attention to cross-device reuse safety and added safety checks to avoid reusing blocks with stale device-mapped pointers. Follow-ups: auto-sizing policy for reuse pools (ENG-4902) and improved heuristics for pin duration prediction.
